chapter: Teddy Wilson bands and Cafe Society
title: The Pump Room in Chicago and the agency tug of war
summary: The Wilson group leaves Cafe Society for an eight-week Pump Room date arranged by William Morris.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: We went uptown and then there became a tug of war between booking agents and between MCA and William Morris Agency and John Kirby (phonetic) [with] was the William Morris Agency, and -- no, the other one.
MCA. And William Morris was trying to

get the account, so they called on Teddy from William Morris Agency to go to the Pump Room in Chicago and we left the Cafe Society Uptown and Barney and Jimmy got mad with us because we left and in that band was Bill Coleman and J. C. and then we augmented with George James and Benny Morton, for the Pump Room, where we had to wear white tails.
So we got the gig for the office and then they let us go.
After you had gotten them in there?

Yeah, yeah. Chauncey Olman was our lawyer. He was the only lawyer for black celebrities like Billy Daniels, Pearl Bailey and Teddy and whatnot and his brother had an orchestra who followed us. All of the employees at the Pump Room were surprised that we weren't going to stay on because there was no, you know, no time limit.
Yeah, yeah, but we had already secured the contract with William Morris.
